title: Python RAG quickstart (FastAPI): ingestion worker, vector adapter, caching defaults
author: Sabrina James
body:
Summary: Adds the first production-shaped Python RAG template to redwood-quickstarts using FastAPI for the query service plus a separate ingestion worker. Includes a vector store adapter layer (default: Postgres + pgvector via SQLAlchemy) and safe caching defaults for embeddings + retrieval results. This template is intended to be opinionated but extensible, and aligns with the telemetry contract v1 (request/tenant correlation, trace attributes, token usage fields, error taxonomy). Motivation: We have repeated onboarding failures where users get a demo working but immediately run into missing timeouts/retries, no correlation IDs, noisy logs, and ad-hoc ingestion scripts. This PR establishes a consistent baseline: (1) an HTTP service with health checks/graceful shutdown, (2) a background ingestion pipeline with idempotency, (3) configurable vector DB backend, (4) caching and backpressure defaults, and (5) out-of-the-box observability wiring.

What’s included: FastAPI RAG service: /v1/query endpoint that performs retrieval + generation (supports streaming via Redwood SDK), /healthz and /readyz endpoints, request ID generation + propagation, structured JSON logs, and basic config layering (env -> .env local -> defaults) with typed settings. Ingestion worker: separate process that ingests documents from a local directory (default) or a URL list, chunks content, generates embeddings via Redwood API, and upserts into the vector store with stable document IDs. Supports incremental re-runs (skip unchanged by content hash), and a small concurrency limiter to avoid tripping rate limits. Vector store adapter: interface + default pgvector implementation; adapter surface kept minimal (upsert_embeddings, query_top_k, delete_by_source). Adds clear extension points for other backends without coupling FastAPI handlers to a specific library. Caching defaults: in-memory TTL cache for embeddings (dedupe repeated chunks during ingestion) and retrieval results (keyed by normalized query + top_k + filters) with short TTL to avoid staleness; caching is opt-out and bounded to control memory. Observability: OpenTelemetry tracing for inbound requests and outbound Redwood SDK calls, trace attributes for model/route/tenant/request_id, counters + histograms for latency and errors, and log correlation fields.

Config & env vars: Introduces consistent env vars for the Python template (mirrors the cross-template contract drafts): REDWOOD_API_KEY (required), REDWOOD_BASE_URL (optional), REDWOOD_MODEL (default for generation), REDWOOD_EMBEDDING_MODEL (default for ingestion), REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_S (default 30), REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES (default 2), REDWOOD_RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_MS (default 200), RAG_TOP_K (default 5), RAG_CHUNK_SIZE (default 800), RAG_CHUNK_OVERLAP (default 100), VECTORSTORE_URL (default postgres://...), VECTORSTORE_SCHEMA (default rag), CACHE_ENABLED (default true), CACHE_TTL_S (default 60), OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (optional), LOG_LEVEL (default info). Note: .env is supported for local dev, but README explicitly warns against committing it; .env.example added.

Implementation notes: Ingestion uses a simple asyncio worker loop to keep dependencies small; avoids Celery/RQ in v1 to reduce setup time (<15 min goal). Uses SQLAlchemy + pgvector for the default vector store, with schema init handled by a small migration script in templates/python/rag/scripts/init_db.py. The query path applies a prompt-injection aware context formatter: retrieved docs are wrapped with explicit delimiters and “untrusted content” guidance; the system prompt instructs the model to treat retrieved context as data and to ignore instructions inside it. Tooling: added Makefile targets (make dev, make ingest, make test, make lint), Dockerfile for app and worker, and a minimal docker-compose that brings up postgres+pgvector for local runs.

Changed areas (high-level): templates/python/rag/ (new): app/ (FastAPI service), worker/ (ingestion), vectorstore/ (adapter + pgvector impl), observability/ (otel setup + helpers), scripts/ (init_db, ingest CLI), deploy/ (Dockerfile, compose), docs/ (README + troubleshooting). templates/python/shared/ (new): config loader, logging helpers, request_id middleware, error taxonomy. root: CI hooks updated for Python lint/type checks on new template.

Illustrative snippets: Request ID + trace propagation: `request_id = request.headers.get("x-request-id") or str(uuid4()); response.headers["x-request-id"] = request_id; span.set_attribute("app.request_id", request_id)`; Retrieval cache key normalization: `key = sha256(f"{q_norm}|{top_k}|{filter_json}".encode()).hexdigest()`; Vector adapter surface: `class VectorStore(Protocol): async def upsert(self, items: list[EmbeddingItem]) -> None; async def query(self, query_embedding: list[float], top_k: int, filters: dict[str, str]) -> list[Hit]`.

Testing: Adds unit tests for chunking, cache bounds, and adapter query serialization; adds a minimal integration test (skipped by default) that runs against a local pgvector instance and verifies query returns expected doc IDs. CI runs ruff/black/mypy and unit tests.

Rollout / follow-ups: This PR intentionally keeps ingestion sources minimal (folder + URL list). We’ll add S3/GCS connectors and richer metadata filters in follow-up PRs once the contract settles. Telemetry contract validation hooks will be added in ENG-2845 wiring across templates.

Checklist: [x] README includes setup, local run, Docker run, and troubleshooting; [x] Health checks + graceful shutdown; [x] Timeouts/retries set via env and defaulted sanely; [x] Structured logs with request_id + tenant; [x] OTel traces + metrics wired; [x] Secrets guidance (.env.example + warnings); [x] Clear extension points for vector store backends; [x] Caching bounded + documented; [x] No PII logged by default.

Links: Linear ENG-2842 (RAG template), ENG-2845 (telemetry contract v1).
conversation:
Monica Patel (review): The overall shape looks good and matches the SDK guidance. Two requests: (1) make sure streaming uses the standardized timeout/retry helper (or at least the same defaults), and (2) I don’t love that we log exception repr() for upstream API failures because it can include prompt fragments. Can we map to an error_class and keep raw payloads out of logs by default? Sabrina James (author): +1. I updated the Redwood client wrapper to use the shared retry defaults and changed error logging to `error_class`, `error_code`, `status_code`, and `request_id` only; full exception text only at DEBUG with an explicit `LOG_SENSITIVE_DEBUG=true` gate for local dev.

Wei Chen (review): README is strong, but the quickstart flow should emphasize “ingest first, then query” and include the expected success output for each command. Also please align env var names with the naming thread (REDWOOD_* and RAG_* prefixes). Sabrina James (author): Updated README with a step-by-step flow and added “Expected output” blocks. Renamed TEMPLATE_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY and cleaned up the remaining mismatches.

Marcus Lin (review): Security: we should include explicit guidance that retrieved docs are untrusted, and the prompt should instruct the model not to follow instructions from retrieval context. Also please ensure we don’t emit document text into logs/traces. Sabrina James (author): Added “untrusted context” language in the system prompt and in docs, and ensured we only log document IDs + source metadata. Also removed any span attributes that contained raw content (now only counts, sizes, and IDs).

Logan Wright (review): Observability: please set trace attributes that Console will expect (tenant, request_id, route/model) and keep cardinality controlled. Also add a counter for vectorstore query failures and a histogram for retrieval latency. Sabrina James (author): Implemented `app.tenant_id` (from x-tenant-id header) + `app.request_id`, `redwood.model`, `redwood.route`, `rag.top_k`. Added `rag.retrieval.latency_ms` histogram and `rag.vectorstore.errors` counter. Avoided adding query text to attributes.

Sean Gallagher (review): SRE nits: /readyz should fail if vector store is unreachable; /healthz can be shallow. Also add a bounded concurrency semaphore around ingestion embedding calls so users don’t accidentally DDoS themselves / hit 429 storms. Sabrina James (author): Done. /readyz now checks DB connection + a simple SELECT 1 and vector extension presence. Added ingestion semaphore and documented how to tune concurrency.

CI notes: Initial run failed on mypy due to missing types for pgvector; pinned stubs and added a small wrapper to keep typing clean. One flake in integration test was resolved by making it opt-in in CI (unit tests always run).

Approvals: Monica Patel approved; Wei Chen approved; Marcus Lin approved; Logan Wright approved; Sean Gallagher approved.

Merge: Squash merged by Sabrina James once CI was green and requested changes addressed.
commits: templates/python/rag: add FastAPI service skeleton + query endpoint
ingestion worker: chunking, embeddings, idempotent upserts
observability: OTel traces/metrics + structured logging middleware
ci: add ruff/black/mypy targets for template
release_notes: Adds Python RAG quickstart template with FastAPI query service + ingestion worker, default pgvector backend, bounded caching, and OTel/structured logging wired to the quickstart telemetry contract v1.
